exposure: induction of labor with a Foley catheter
outcome: Maternal morbidity (intrapartum and postpartum infection rates)
cohort: 553 women with uncomplicated prolonged pregnancies (≥41(+5) weeks of gestation) at Helsinki University Hospital between January 2011 and January 2012
finding: While Foley catheter induction of labor in prolonged pregnancy did not increase maternal or perinatal morbidity compared to spontaneous labor onset, it was associated with a significantly increased cesarean section rate, especially among nulliparous women.
mod_finding: Foley catheter induction of labor in prolonged pregnancy was associated with a considerably increased cesarean section rate.
